tagline: Costa Rica's Pacific luxury-resort coast and the Gulf of Nicoya ferry system — eco-credentials and resort density that fit a zero-emission foiling fleet like a glove.
summary: The Gulf of Papagayo anchors Costa Rica's highest-end Pacific resort cluster (Four Seasons, Andaz, Marina Papagayo) just north of Liberia's international airport, while the broader Nicoya Peninsula is reached across the Gulf of Nicoya by a busy car-ferry system (Puntarenas to Paquera/Naranjo). Demand splits cleanly into luxury resort transfers and yacht movements in the north, and utilitarian peninsula access in the south where the land route is a long detour. Costa Rica's national zero-carbon brand makes a silent electric-foiling layer not just operationally attractive but a marketing asset for the destination. Pioneer II handles resort and gulf-crossing legs; Quanta LR opens longer Pacific runs toward the Quepos / Manuel Antonio coast.

use_cases.title: Papagayo resort & marina transfers
use_cases.body: Silent, zero-wake foiling transfers between Marina Papagayo, the Four Seasons and Andaz resorts, and Playas del Coco — a signature on-water arrival inside a marine-protected bay that replaces diesel tenders.

use_cases.title: Gulf of Nicoya fast passenger crossing
use_cases.body: A clean, fast foot-passenger link across the Gulf of Nicoya alongside the Puntarenas–Paquera car ferries, collapsing the long land detour into a smooth direct hop to the Nicoya Peninsula beach towns.

use_cases.title: Liberia airport-to-resort sea shuttle
use_cases.body: A short premium sea transfer connecting the Liberia (LIR) catchment to the Papagayo resort coast, turning the final leg of a long-haul luxury trip into part of the experience.

use_cases.title: Pacific-coast day-charter & line-haul
use_cases.body: Longer experiential runs down the Pacific coast toward Tamarindo, Quepos and Manuel Antonio — corridors served only by slow road today — opened up by the hybrid range of Quanta LR.

journeys.name: Marina Papagayo <-> Playas del Coco / resort coast
journeys.today: Diesel resort tenders and sportfishing launches across the bay.
journeys.with_navier: A silent, zero-wake foiling transfer in a marine-protected bay.

journeys.name: Puntarenas <-> Paquera (Gulf of Nicoya)
journeys.today: Car ferry, ~1h20 crossing on a fixed 4–6 sailing schedule; long land detour by road.
journeys.with_navier: A fast, clean foiling alternative for foot passengers across the gulf.

journeys.name: Papagayo <-> Quepos / Manuel Antonio
journeys.today: Long Pacific-coast corridor served only by road.
journeys.with_navier: A hybrid line-haul down the Pacific coast that road can't match for time or experience.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The resort and gulf legs sit comfortably inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope — Marina Papagayo to Playas del Coco (~3 nm) and the Puntarenas–Paquera Gulf of Nicoya crossing (~12 nm) — on protected water ideal for quiet, zero-wake foiling that aligns with Costa Rica's carbon-neutral brand and the Gulf's marine-protected zones.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Quanta LR's ~2,000 nm hybrid range, with no shore-charging dependency, unlocks the long Pacific-coast corridors toward Tamarindo, Quepos and Manuel Antonio (~130 nm) that are served only by slow road today.

competitive_landscape: Today: car ferries (Coonatramar, Naviera Tambor) plus resort tender boats and sportfishing charters; no clean fast-passenger layer.
seasonality: Dry season Dec-Apr peak; Papagayo winds strongest Dec-Mar — a foiling hull's stability is an advantage in chop.
regulatory_note: MarViva / SINAC marine-protected zones in the Gulf of Papagayo; clean propulsion eases permitting.
